content.title: About
content.content: Beans and white rice are a classic combination of legumes and grains used in cuisines worldwide. Beans provide protein, fiber, and micronutrients, while white rice supplies quick‑digesting carbohydrates for energy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The bean‑rice pairing is considered a complete protein source because together they supply all essential amino acids.
Dried beans can be stored for several years, and rice can last up to a year when kept dry.
In many cultures beans and rice are cooked together in one pot, enhancing flavor and simplifying preparation.
White rice is often fortified with vitamins and iron to replace nutrients lost during milling.

items.title: Rich plant protein
items.content: Beans contain about 20 g of protein per 100 g, making them a key protein source for vegetarians.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The fiber in beans promotes regular bowel movements and helps stabilize blood sugar levels.

items.title: Quick energy source
items.content: White rice is rapidly digested, providing a fast glucose boost, especially useful after intense exercise.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: Beans are a good source of iron and magnesium, essential for blood formation and muscle function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Both beans and white rice are naturally low in saturated fat, fitting well into low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Beans contain phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption; soaking and sprouting help mitigate this.

items.title: Lectins
items.content: Certain beans have lectins that may cause gastrointestinal discomfort if not cooked thoroughly.

items.title: High glycemic index of rice
items.content: White rice has a high glycemic index, which can cause rapid blood sugar spikes in people with diabetes.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: A small percentage of individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Soak beans for 6–8 hours, then boil until tender. Rinse white rice and cook with a 1:2 rice‑to‑water ratio. Combine them in salads, soups, pilafs, or as a side dish to meat and vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry beans in an airtight container in a cool, dry place for up to 2 years. Keep white rice in a sealed package away from moisture and light for up to 12 months. Discard any beans or rice that develop off‑odors, mold, or insect infestation.
